checks.name: CONTROL: S + Q = N/P exactly, and S_same + S_opp = S
checks.detail: exact Fraction identity at every n = 4..46, 0 mismatches. Integer accumulation throughout, so there is no rounding to hide in.

checks.name: CONTROL: N/P, S and Q agree with the committed decomposition witness
checks.detail: exact Fraction equality on n = 4..46 (43 levels), 0 mismatches. This probe reaches S and Q by a different route (Lam-centric, integer) than the witness did (pair-dict, Fraction).

checks.name: TELESCOPING case 1 (same sign): slope is a DENSITY, 0 <= slope <= 1
checks.detail: 0 violations over n = 4..46. delta(t) = D(t)-D(t+1) in {0,1}, so the same-sign slope is the fraction of drop sites in [u,v). max over range = 2/3.

checks.name: TELESCOPING case 2 (opposite sign): |slope| <= D(0)/g
checks.detail: 0 violations over n = 4..46. The two side-telescopings share the same total D(0), which cancels; what is left is a difference of two drop-site counts, each in [0, D(0)]. This is the case the header called out of reach of the identity, and it is not.

checks.name: ...and case 2 is SHARP: the bound is attained, not slack
checks.detail: max over opposite-sign edges of |slope|*g/D(0) = 1 (exactly 1) over n = 4..46. A bound one cannot improve per-edge; everything further must come from averaging.

checks.name: CONTROL: the case-2 detector fires against a halved bound D(0)/2g
checks.detail: 147986 violations of |slope| <= D(0)/2g over the same edges, so the check above is comparing something.

checks.name: REFUTED (mine): omega-weight on opposite-sign edges does NOT shrink
checks.detail: w_opp over n = 39..46: ['0.461', '0.462', '0.461', '0.4583', '0.4544', '0.4498', '0.4449', '0.4404'] -- it peaks near n = 40 and sits around 0.44, not shrinking. I predicted it would vanish. It does not, so the opposite-sign case had to be handled rather than dismissed, which is what case 2 above does.

checks.name: REFUTED (mine): S_opp is not negative -- it crosses zero and SATURATES
checks.detail: S_opp over the same range: ['0.1152', '0.1171', '0.1181', '0.1185', '0.1184', '0.1182', '0.1181', '0.1183']. It is negative below n ~ 18, crosses, and flattens near 0.118 -- about 36% of S at n = 46. I predicted it would subtract from S. For n >= 19 it adds.

checks.name: REFUTED (mine): lambda_1 > 2 D(0) FAILS pointwise on the omega support
checks.detail: omega-weight on lambda_1 <= 2 D(0): ['0.124', '0.112', '0.104', '0.0988', '0.0976', '0.0991', '0.103', '0.107'] -- around 10%, not 0; min margin lambda_1 - 2 D(0) = -6. Under VKLS the ratio -> pi/2, but that is about TYPICAL diagrams and the omega-measure charges atypical ones (a square has lambda_1 = D(0)). The pointwise form of the headroom argument is DEAD; only an averaged form can survive.

checks.name: SURVIVES: inflation E[slope|same]/E[global density|same] stays far under pi/2
checks.detail: max over n = 4..46 is 0.493752 against pi/2 = 1.5708; last eight ['0.4356', '0.4437', '0.4525', '0.4618', '0.4709', '0.4795', '0.4872', '0.4938'] -- rising, and its limit is NOT determined by this range. Below 1 throughout, i.e. the omega-chosen intervals drop LESS than the diagram's own average, not more.

checks.name: SURVIVES: the AVERAGED form of the dead pointwise condition holds for n >= 5
checks.detail: E_omega[D(0)/lambda_1] < 1/2 uninterrupted on n = 5..46; the sole exception anywhere is n = 4 at 25/48 = 0.5208, where lambda = (2,2) has lambda_1 = D(0). Last eight: ['0.3918', '0.3899', '0.3881', '0.3863', '0.3847', '0.3834', '0.3824', '0.3819'], heading for the VKLS 1/pi = 0.31831. This is what must replace 'lambda_1 > 2 D(0) pointwise', and effective Plancherel concentration for lambda_1 is where it would come from.

checks.name: MEASURED: the case-2 bound is ~an order of magnitude too weak as it stands
checks.detail: at n = 46: bound B_opp = 2 E[D(0)/g ; opp] = 0.614748 against the true S_opp = 0.118273, a factor of 5.198. Combined with the trivial same-sign bound 2*w_same = 1.11927 the total exceeds 1, so the per-edge bounds ALONE do not close it. They are elementary and deterministic, which the effective CLT is not -- but averaging is still required on BOTH sides.
